cards.explanation: The answer is whether the charges are true. The high priest asks Stephen, “Are these charges true?” No small talk, no warm-up, just a question you could answer with one word. Hold onto that, friends, because Stephen has a whole lot more than one word coming. The question was about the charges, and that's all it was.

The answer is Abraham, friends. Stephen says, “The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran…” Abraham is the man Stephen calls “our father.” Starting here is like opening a family reunion speech with the great-great-grandparents.

The two answers are descendants and child. Stephen says God promised to give possession of the land “…to Abraham and his descendants…” So the promise reaches past Abraham to the people who would come after him. Abraham himself has no inheritance there, not even a foot of ground. God made the promise “…even though he did not yet have a child.” That's a big promise to carry around with an empty nursery.

The answer is the land God brought Abraham to, friends. God says the descendants “…will come forth and worship Me in this place.” Back in verse 4, Stephen said God brought Abraham “…into this land where you are now living.” So the worship is promised for the very land the council is standing in.

The answer is jealousy, friends. Stephen says, “Because the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph, they sold him as a slave into Egypt.” The twelve patriarchs come from Jacob, and the ones jealous of Joseph are his brothers. And Stephen adds right away, “But God was with him”

The answer is ruler over Egypt and all his household. Stephen says God gave Joseph favor and wisdom in Pharaoh's sight, and Pharaoh “…appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his household.” Think about that climb, friends. Sold as a slave, then running the whole country, and Stephen says it was because God was with him.

The answer is False, friends. Stephen says the new king “…knew nothing of Joseph…” and he “…exploited our people and oppressed our fathers…” He forced them to abandon their infants so they would die. That's a hard thing to hear, so it's worth pausing on.

The answer is deliver, friends. Stephen says Moses “…assumed his brothers would understand that God was using him to deliver them, but they did not.” Moses had a whole picture in his head and nobody else had seen it yet. It's like walking into the room sure everybody got the memo, and nobody got the memo.

The answer is the land of Midian. Stephen says, “At this remark, Moses fled to the land of Midian, where he lived as a foreigner and had two sons.” That remark had two parts: who made Moses ruler and judge, and whether he wanted to kill the man like he killed the Egyptian. That's a long way to travel because of a comment, friends.

The answer is redeemer, friends. Stephen says God sent Moses “…to be their ruler and redeemer through the angel who appeared to him in the bush.” The man asked who made Moses ruler and judge, and Stephen's answer is that God sent him. The same Moses they pushed aside is the one God sent to them.

The answer is like Moses, friends. Stephen says, “This is the same Moses who told the Israelites, ‘God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.’” So Moses is the one speaking, and he says the prophet will be like him. Stephen puts that line right in the middle of his speech about Moses.

The answer is obey, friends. Stephen says, “…our fathers refused to obey him. Instead, they rejected him and in their hearts turned back to Egypt.” Moses received living words to pass on, and the fathers refused to obey him. That's a big gap between what they were given and what they did.

The answer is into exile beyond Babylon. In the quote from the book of the prophets, God says, “Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Babylon.” Stephen is quoting about the idols they made to worship. It's a heavy line, friends, and Stephen doesn't soften it.
